description: An 8-bit hit voice: one oscillator crossfading between a pulse wave, a falling sawtooth and pitched noise, with a pitch bend and a pair of filters

params.text: Sets the pitch, from 54 semitones below C4 at 261.63Hz to 54 semitones above it
Bends the pitch across the note, upwards as it is turned up and downwards as it is turned down; the amount follows the cube of the setting, so small settings do very little
Crossfades the oscillator from a pulse wave at its minimum, through a falling sawtooth and then pitched noise, and back to the pulse wave at its maximum
Sets the width of the pulse wave, from 1% to 99%
Sets how long the envelope holds at full level before the release begins, from 1ms to 250ms
Sets how long the envelope takes to fall in a straight line from full level to nothing, from 0ms to 250ms
Sets the corner of the high-pass filter at the output; at 0% the filter is out of the signal path altogether
Opens the low-pass filter at the output; at 0% the filter is almost shut and very little gets through, and at 100% it is at its widest

inputs.text: Adds to the pitch set by FREQ at one volt per octave, read at the moment the trigger arrives
Adds to the bend set by SLIDE, a tenth of its travel per volt, read at the moment the trigger arrives
Adds to the crossfade set by BLND, three tenths of its travel per volt
Adds to the width set by PW, a tenth of its travel per volt
Doubles the time set by HOLD per volt and halves it per volt below zero, read at the moment the trigger arrives
Doubles the time set by REL per volt and halves it per volt below zero, read at the moment the trigger arrives
Starts a note when it rises past 2V, and has to fall back below 0.1V before another note can start

outputs.text: The envelope as a voltage from 0V to 10V, quantised to 127 steps
The voice, quantised to 127 steps and clipped at 5V either way

notes: LPF comes up at 0%, which closes the low-pass filter almost completely and leaves next to nothing at the output. Turn it up before expecting to hear anything.
With nothing patched into TRIG the envelope is held wide open and the oscillator drones. It only shapes the sound once a trigger cable is in.
The pitch, the bend, the hold, the release and both filter settings are read once, at the moment TRIG fires; moving those controls during a note has no effect until the next one.
